newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegro foreign minister dies in car crash.
newsitem.headline: Montenegro foreign minister dies in car crash.

text.p: Janko Jeknic, foreign minister of the Yugoslav republic of Montenegro, died on Friday in a car crash, his secretary said.
Reached by telephone in the Montenegrin capital Podgorica, she confirmed reports that Jeknic was killed in the accident on the Podgorica-Danilovgrad road near Komanski Most.
The Montenegrin news agency Montena-fax said Jeknic's car collided with a bus that had stopped on the side of the road. A woman passenger in the car was seriously injured, it said.

Tanjug, the Yugoslav news agency, said Jeknic was 46 years old. He had a university degree in economics and served as head of protocol and consul for economic affairs in the Yugoslav consulate in Milan, Italy, before becoming foreign minister.

Montenegro, a small mountainous territory flanking the Adriatic Sea, and the larger, more populous Serbia are the only republics left in federal Yugoslavia after the secession of four others in 1991-92.
The moderate Montenegrin leadership has been critical of leftist Serbia's resistance to democratic reform and privatisation, fearing this will prolong Yugoslavia's international isolation.
